subject: Observability export safety rails & tracehook playbook
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.example.com
Cc: security-team@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-04 09:12 -0700
Subject: Observability export requirements and a couple of questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this — we kicked off our internal review of the private deployment telemetry path and have a few gating questions before we proceed with the network firewall exceptions and procurement for a dedicated forwarder. High level: AcmeHealth needs assurance that anything leaving our VPC will not contain unredacted PHI or user-identifiable fields, and we also need to capture trace correlation IDs for end-to-end latency SLOs.

Specifically: 
- Can Redwood's forwarder perform pre-export scrubbing with configurable regex/JSON-path rules and a validation pass that rejects batches with PHI-like artifacts?
- How do you handle tracehook propagation and the preservation of our internal span IDs when you run in a co-located forwarder vs. a sidecar?
- For audit, we need signed receipts of successful export deliveries (not just 200 OKs). Do you support a proof-of-transfer artifact?

Attached is a short summary of our regulatory checklist. Would appreciate a short plan and any sample configs so we can start our security review.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Security Engineer — AcmeHealth

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.example.com
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-10-04 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export requirements and a couple of questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of our approach and an outline of next steps below.

Short answers: 
1) Yes — our on-prem forwarder supports a pre-export transform pipeline with multiple stages: (a) structural normalization (JSON schema enforcement), (b) rule-based redaction (regex + JSONPath), and (c) a lightweight ML-backed detector for PHI tokens. You can opt to have the pipeline fail a batch and hold it for manual review.
2) Trace propagation: we preserve incoming trace/span IDs. When deployed as a sidecar the agent attaches minimal metadata and forwards enriched spans; in dedicated forwarder mode we accept and forward raw wire-format spans while mapping headers to the same correlation ID field. We also provide a small instrumentation shim if you need header-mapping for legacy agents.
3) Proof-of-transfer: we emit compact signed receipts (HMAC + timestamp + sequence id) stored in an encrypted ledger on the forwarder. Those receipts are available via an API and can be pushed to your S3 or pulled over an authenticated channel for audits.

Proposed immediate plan (week-by-week):
- Week 0: Exchange PII/PHI regex profiles and a sample dataset (redacted).
- Week 1: Deploy a sidecar stub in your staging cluster, run synthetic traceflows and export validation (no egress allowed yet).
- Week 2: Enable egress to Redwood test-collector with scrub rules active; collect receipts and error logs.
- Week 3: Run a compliance acceptance test (SOC-like checklist) and handover runbook.

I've attached three starter artifacts: a scrub profile template (acme_scrub_profiles.yaml), a forwarder runbook (forwarder_runbook.pdf) and a small patch for tracehook instrumentation we recommend (tracehook_instrumentation_patch.diff).

Can you confirm who on your team will own the acceptance checklist and the VPN/Egress rule ticket? Once I have that we can schedule the staging deploy.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.example.com, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-10-05 09:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export requirements and a couple of questions

Alice / Rafael — adding a few non-negotiables from the security acceptance side so we can align expectations: 

1) Scrubbing policy QA: please note the scrub pipeline supports three modes — safe-redact (irreversible mask), reversible-tokenize (for cases where Acme wants to rehydrate within their private environment), and reject-on-detect. The default for regulated fields must be safe-redact. We'll provide a test harness to validate mask correctness against your sample corpus.

2) Retention mapping: exports to Redwood-hosted collectors must respect Acme retention TTLs. For Private deployments where the forwarder sends to a customer-managed SIEM (e.g., Splunk HEC inside the VPC), we require a documented retention contract and evidence that logs are not checkpointed beyond the agreed TTL.

3) Network posture: egress must be limited to a narrow set of IPs/CIDRs during test and a rotated set of destinations for prod. We'll provide suggested firewall rules and a watchlist for unexpected endpoints.

4) Trace integrity: if you choose the dedicated forwarder, include a header-preservation test in the acceptance checklist; for sidecar mode we'll require a signed integration test (included in the runbook).

Operational notes: buffering strategies differ — sidecar mode buffers to ephemeral disk and favors low-latency pass-through; dedicated forwarder can buffer more aggressively but requires disk encryption at rest. In either case we enforce backpressure behavior: if the forwarder cannot deliver, it will flip to disk-buffering-first then halt non-essential telemetry and raise a high-severity alert.

I've updated the runbook with our suggested firewall rule set and a sample acceptance checklist (see forwarder_runbook.pdf). Rafael — please make sure the runbook references the HEC token rotation cadence and proof-of-transfer API endpoints.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security PM — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-10-06 08:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability export requirements and a couple of questions

Hi all — operational checklist and a few implementation specifics below (pulled from our staging playbook):

- Deployment options: Kubernetes DaemonSet sidecar vs. dedicated forwarder (K8s Deployment behind a Service). Recommendation: start with DaemonSet in staging to validate scrubbing, then switch to dedicated forwarder in pre-prod to verify throughput and disk-buffering behavior.

- Scrub profiles: attached acme_scrub_profiles.yaml contains regex examples for MRNs, SSNs, email addresses, and a JSONPath section that targets known user object fields (user.email, user.contact.*). We'll iterate these with your SREs.

- Sampling & metrics: we expose an exporter-metrics endpoint on the forwarder (Prometheus format) with counters for accepted/blocked/failed batches, last-probe-timestamp, and proof_receipt_count. Add these to your SIEM for operational dashboards.

- Tracehook specifics: the patch (tracehook_instrumentation_patch.diff) adds an optional header X-ACME-SPAN that maps to Redwood's internal trace_id preservation field. In dedicated mode the forwarder will not rewrite span IDs; in sidecar mode the shim ensures header passthrough.

- Proof-of-transfer: receipts are signed with a key we rotate monthly by default. For compliance you can also request that receipts be forwarded to your internal archival endpoint (S3/GCS) via an encrypted channel — see forwarder_runbook.pdf, section 4.3.

- Acceptance test: we recommend three test vectors: (1) synthetic PHI-laden logs that must be redacted, (2) traceflow verification to validate 1:1 correlation across services, (3) failure-mode test where downstream is unreachable and the forwarder demonstrates buffer-to-disk with receipt of queued batches.

I'll volunteer to run the staging deploy with your SRE if you can provide cluster access (read-only with the ability to create namespaces and DaemonSets). Suggested timeslot: Wed 2026-10-13 10:00 PT.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Observability Lead — Redwood Inference
